verdict.rationale: Auth0 documents giving each agent its own identity. It also documents machine-to-machine client-credentials identities that authenticate as the application rather than a user, with scopes and granular permissions for M2M communications. That covers per-agent identity and narrow scoping, but nothing in the evidence shows instant revocation of an agent's credentials or tokens. Missing for 10: documented instant revocation of an agent's identity or tokens, a per-agent least-privilege configuration walkthrough, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give each agent its own least-privilege machine identity with narrowly scoped permissions and instant revocation, instead of sharing a human's credentials

citations.quote: Give each agent a unique digital identity for more secure access to APIs, apps, and MCP servers.
the system must authenticate and authorize the application instead of a user
Handle authorization using scopes and granular permissions, whether it's for first-party apps, third-party integrations, or Machine-to-Machine communications.
Applications authenticate themselves to Auth0 via their Client Id and Client Secret. Auth0 verifies the information and responds with an Access Token.
